One grey-green vase with pink flushes in a high-fired style could be Ruskin but the base is not shown.

lots.guide_summary: All AUD, no conversion. Six Gowans SOLD hammers for comparable mixed china lots naming Royal Winton, Royal Doulton or Carlton Ware, $45 to $110 (most $60 to $65), plus one passed-in group (same lot sold for $45 a week later). No asking evidence survives. The Ruskin result (GBP 1,500, 2015) is kept only as an upside reference for the unmarked vase and is outside the range.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD = $45 hammer (Gowans, July 2026). 45 / 1.22 = 36.89, round down to $35 hammer ($42.70 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $60 hammer in a Tasmanian room (the median of the Gowans results); less about 20% seller commission and fees = $48 net, no postage (local room). 48 / 2.44 = 19.67, round down to $15. Flipping a mixed china lot barely pays; the only real upside is the vase if it is a marked Ruskin.
lots.confidence_reason: Royal Doulton Clairmont and Royal Winton marks read, and six Gowans SOLD results (API JSON opened) in the last 12 months, but they are mixed lots with undescribed contents, so none is the same item. The vase base is not shown.
